blockers.title: 权限 await 完成后，旧 operation 在 stop 结算后仍首次发出原生页面副作用

contract.distinction: stop does not undo already-issued side effects; this browser API is first issued after stop, so that exception does not apply

blockers.cause: Message ingress captures owner, but operation() does not receive that identity. It awaits real permission state, then reads mutable active/tabId/documentId. goto calls tabs.update even when active is null; owner is captured after the await. The reply fence at line 59 prevents a reply, not the newly issued effect. Other methods read active.runId and could misattribute a stale continuation to a newly admitted run; only the goto/stop case was dynamically reproduced here.
blockers.evidence: independentProbe.runs: both actual versions; permissions result true after stop, native tabs.update invoked with active=null, requested destination actually received by HTTP server and committed in the tab. Old run remains stopped exactly once, no old reply, later valid run succeeds. The probe uses explicit in-memory scheduling instrumentation and delegates to native APIs without replacing results.
reproduction: Restore/hash-check the exact 711f source, not the author's now-changing live files.
Launch the exact native binary with a fresh profile and unchanged extension fixture; initialize the real owned form tab.
Call the actual chrome.permissions.contains, schedule ordinary harness.stop() in a microtask before its promise resolution, then return that real promise unchanged.
Run await page.goto(params.url); record order through a thin delegate to actual chrome.tabs.update; observe the actual server destination and tab URL.
The full executed stdin script and selected raw measured values are preserved in independentProbe.
blockers.minimalFix: Pass immutable owner/run/host/sandbox epoch and target identity from admission into operation. After permission and every intervening await, revalidate the captured owner and target immediately before each native Chrome dispatch and before adopting a new navigation document. Use captured runId, never the next run's global active. Once closed, reject the stale continuation without new page effects; do not attempt to undo already-issued effects.
blockers.requiredValidation: Bounded native stop, deadline, host-close, and old-authorization-completion-after-new-run cases on both versions, with native permission results, real HTTP/page effects and their order, exactly one old terminal state, no effect/identity adoption from old run, and a successful subsequent run. Freeze a new source/evidence candidate for independent review; do not alter old 46 PASS or old counterproof.

If the realm is retired instead, distinguish browser-owned realm destruction from explicit revoke, and independently prove it and target absence. Checking an old opaque Blob from a new opaque origin is not alone a revocation proof.
